title: The Charge of the Light Brigade
summary: Josh and Chuck (iHeart Intro voice) explain the Charge of the Light Brigade during the Crimean War. They cover the war's origins in the Ottoman-Russian religious dispute and Russia's occupation of Wallachia and Moldavia, the British and French alliance landing in Crimea in 1854, the Battle of the Alma, the siege of Sevastopol, and the Battle of Balaklava. At Balaklava, the Highlanders stop a Russian cavalry attack at Causeway Heights and a garbled order from Lord Raglan sends the Light Brigade under Lucan and Cardigan into the Valley of Death, with heavy casualties. They discuss Tennyson's 1854 poem, Russell's reporting, the Cardigan sweater, Thin Red Line, the veterans' poverty, and film adaptations. The episode ends with listener mail about the hosts' disagreements.
topics: Tennyson poem The Charge of the Light Brigade
Errol Flynn Charge of the Light Brigade film

entities.name: The Charge of the Heavy Brigade

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the rare war battle episode on the Charge of the Light Brigade and the Tennyson poem.

segments.title: Origins of the Crimean War
segments.summary: Overview of the Crimean War from 1853 to 1856, its death toll mostly from disease, and the nurses Florence Nightingale and Mary Seacole. The war began over Christian holy sites in the Ottoman Empire, then Russia occupied Wallachia and Moldavia. Britain and France responded, sent warships, and declared war in 1854. The Russians withdrew in July 1854, but the alliance chose to attack Crimea.

segments.title: Allied landing in Crimea
segments.summary: The Allied forces chose Crimea for naval and land strategy, and landed in September 1854 to march on Sevastopol.

segments.title: Battle of the Alma and the siege of Sevastopol
segments.summary: The Battle of the Alma River was the first major battle, with the Russians retreating. The Allies took a long route around Sevastopol, which gave the Russians time to refortify. The British settled at Balaklava, and the Russians moved troops to cut the road between the sieging forces and Balaklava.

segments.title: Causeway Heights and the Highlanders
segments.summary: Russians attacked artillery positions on Causeway Heights and then Kadikoi. The 93rd Sutherland Highlanders, led by Colin Campbell, used a two-line formation and stopped a Russian cavalry charge with volleys. The hosts also discuss the term thin red line from William Howard Russell's reporting.

segments.title: Wives at the front and cultural tangents
segments.summary: Brief discussion of soldiers' wives traveling to the front during this war, followed by a tangent on war movies.
topics: soldiers' wives in the Crimean War

segments.title: Light versus heavy cavalry
segments.summary: Explanation that the Light Brigade was a fast cavalry unit for scouting and quick orders, while the Heavy Brigade had bigger horses and men for close combat.

segments.title: Heavy Brigade charge and Lord Raglan's order
segments.summary: The Heavy Brigade charged first with about 800 horsemen against about 3,000 Russians. Lord Raglan, commanding from a ridge, sent a vague order, and it was delivered by Captain Lewis Nolan. The messages were confusing and the hosts describe the commanders' poor competence.

segments.title: Lucan and Cardigan
segments.summary: Earl of Lucan and Earl of Cardigan, wealthy officers who bought their commissions and disliked each other, were given the order. Lucan's landlord history is mentioned. Nolan pointed the wrong way, toward a heavily defended Russian position, and the Light Brigade was ordered to charge. The hosts also mention the Cardigan sweater.

segments.title: The charge through the Valley of Death
segments.summary: The roughly 670 Light Brigade riders charged into the Valley of Death under fire from three directions. They captured the central Russian guns, while a French light cavalry unit destroyed another position. Casualties were 110 killed, 160 wounded, and 375 horses killed. Lucan refused to send the Heavy Brigade after them.

segments.title: Legacy: Tennyson's poem and Russell's report
segments.summary: Russell's dispatch describes the charge. Tennyson wrote the poem as Poet Laureate about six weeks after the battle, published in The Examiner. The hosts read the second stanza and discuss Tennyson's poor recording of it.

segments.title: Veterans' poverty and film adaptations
segments.summary: Tennyson and Kipling wrote poems to raise money for destitute Crimean veterans, raising only 24 pounds. Film adaptations are discussed: the 1936 Errol Flynn version and the 1968 satire starring John Gielgud and Vanessa Redgrave.
topics: Kipling Last of the Light Brigade
1968 Charge of the Light Brigade film

segments.title: Listener mail on hosts' disagreements
segments.summary: A listener from Warner Fenn asks whether the hosts have disagreed and cut it. The hosts say they leave disagreements in and mostly agree on big things, with small differences like pickles.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts mention live shows and the email address, then sign off.
